thread:
aj: Heads up — Meridian v3 rollout targeted in ~48h. Product expects a multi-hour canary with an initial 3x token/sec uplift for the first 72h. Need a quick egress & capacity risk check focusing on peering points (SJC, LHR) and regional L4 pools.

aj: ```
current baseline: 110k t/s across fleet
projected canary peak: 330k t/s (3x)
canary window: 72h, ramp steps: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%
model size: ~28B, primary q4_0; fallback float16
SLO: p95 latency < 500ms (tight)
```

sre-oncall: quick q — what GPU mix are we targeting for canary? A100-80 preferred for fallback but can we use L4 in APAC? Any hard region pins?

aj: plan is A100 heavy in US, keep L4 regional in APAC. EU should be A100 if possible for latency. Traffic split est: US 68% / EU 22% / APAC 10%.

cheng: ran a throughput->GPU sketch using our latest q4_0 throughput curves (A100 ~5.8k t/s, L4 ~3.2k t/s). Adding 1.3x safety factor for autoscaler headroom + cold starts.

cheng: ```
peak = 330000 t/s
US_peak = peak * 0.68 = 224400 t/s
EU_peak = peak * 0.22 = 72600 t/s
APAC_peak = peak * 0.10 = 33000 t/s

US_gpus = ceil((224400 / 5800) * 1.3) = ceil(38.69 * 1.3) = 51 A100-eq
EU_gpus = ceil((72600 / 5800) * 1.3) = ceil(12.51 * 1.3) = 17 A100-eq
APAC_gpus = ceil((33000 / 3200) * 1.3) = ceil(10.31 * 1.3) = 14 L4-eq

Total ~= 82 A100-eq -> GPU-hours = 82 * 72 = 5,904 GPU-hours
Add 12% ops & memory contingency -> ~6,613 GPU-hours
```

maria: FYI eu-west1 currently has ~36 A100s free but cold-start (images + cache warm) is ~7-9h. We can commit 18 A100s for the window if we lock them; full EU failover for US traffic is risky.

aj: network: SJC->APAC peering looked noisy yesterday. Are there egress caps or per-conn QPS limits at the edge that could cause throttling at ramp? Also, any CDN/edge caching options to reduce cross-region KV hits?

sre-oncall: network snapshot: SJC peering to SIN and HKG peaked at ~92% utilization during last major window. LHR->APAC looked fine. Mitigations proposed:
1) regionalize APAC traffic to local L4 pool (must pre-provision)
2) enable token-prefix KV cache (reduces cross-region fanout ~20%)
3) pre-warm persistent connections / increase keepalive pools to avoid connection churn at SJC peering

sre-oncall: also opened NET-9104 to coordinate with peering vendor for an ETA on additional capacity if needed.

cheng: cost roughs for budgeting: A100 $3.10/hr, L4 $1.05/hr (reserved). With the mix above (68 A100-eq, 14 L4-eq sim) and 6,613 GPU-hours -> ballpark $21k-$26k for the 72h canary including contingency.

ops-lead: procurement heads-up — please pre-approve up to $35k of incremental spend for the window in case we need to extend or failover. maria, can you lock EU capacity and raise the CAP ticket?

maria: reserving 18 A100s in eu-west1 for the 72h window and filing CAP-4972 to move them into a dedicated reserve. Noted image warm time in the ticket.

aj: action items (short):
- cheng: final GPU mix + LB placement plan by EOD (prefer bias to US A100s to avoid EU cold-start risk)
- maria: complete reservation + CAP-4972; annotate capacity sheet and hold for 96h window
- sre-oncall: flip token-prefix KV cache feature flag for canary, pre-warm SJC peering keepalive pools, and set router soft cap at 75% (hard cap 95%)
- opsbot: generate canary playbook with rollback triggers and on-call escalation

opsbot: canary playbook created: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/meridian-v3-canary (rollback on 3% error spike or 25% latency regression, paging to #eng-oncall). :white_check_mark:

dilrukshi: note about float16 fallback — memory pressure increase observed ~20% on similar models; per-GPU throughput dropped ~8-12% last time. Recommend factoring that into the final numbers and a small additional cache headroom.

cheng: incorporating float16 contingency -> new total ~= 95 A100-eq, GPU-hours ~= 6,840, estimated cost +15% vs prior. Updating the capacity sheet now and will attach to CAP-4972.

aj: thanks. If cheng + maria confirm the final manifest we'll greenlight pre-provision tomorrow 09:00 PT and freeze the traffic rollout schedule. Ping here when CAP-4972 is updated.

sre-oncall: will post final capacity manifest and peering mitigation checklist in ~30m.
